content.title: Customer Success Manager (Japan) at RegASK
content.description: Our Company RegASK is the Agentic AI Regulatory Operating System for life sciences and consumer products companies. We believe the future of regulatory work is not just better intelligence; it is intelligent execution. Powered by vertical AI and backed by a global network of 1,800+ regulatory subject matter experts, RegASK enables organizations to anticipate regulatory change, assess its impact, and orchestrate compliance activities across 160+ markets. Our platform connects regulatory intelligence, decision-making, and workflow execution into a single system designed for modern regulatory teams. Today, organizations use RegASK across Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Safety, Labeling, Packaging, R&D, and Legal to navigate increasing regulatory complexity with greater speed, confidence, and control. By combining agentic AI, human expertise, and enterprise governance, we are helping global companies transform regulatory operations from a reactive function into a strategic business capability. As a fast-growing global company, we are always looking for curious, ambitious people who enjoy solving meaningful problems at the intersection of AI, regulation, and enterprise transformation. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you. Position Overview We are looking for an enthusiastic and bilingual entry-level Customer Success Manager (Japan) who is fluent in Japanese and English to join our growing team. In this client-facing role, you will support the Customer Success team in delivering exceptional service to our Japanese clients. This is a great opportunity for someone looking to grow their career in customer success, client engagement, or account management while working in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. This role will be 50% supporting CX and 50% supporting Sales Responsibilities Support the Singapore-based Customer Success team in managing Japanese client accounts Join client meetings as a bilingual representative, assisting in communication, note-taking, and follow-ups Translate materials (emails, presentations, reports) between Japanese and English to ensure clear understanding Help onboard new Japanese clients and provide support throughout the client journe Coordinate meetings, manage client touchpoints, and ensure timely responses to client inquiries Collaborate with internal teams (e.g. Product, Content, and Regulatory teams) to deliver client requirements Monitor client engagement and help track deliverables, usage, and satisfaction Prepare reports and presentations to support customer reviews and renewal conversation Assist in prospecting activities, such as initial outreach coordination and research, to support team involved in Business Development, Account Management, and Customer Success. Requirements Business-level proficiency in Japanese (spoken and written) Professional proficiency in English 0–2 years of experience in customer-facing roles, internships, or admin support (fresh graduates are welcome) Strong communication, organization, and coordination skills Team-oriented, proactive, and eager to learn Comfortable using/or learning digital tools like Zoom, Confluence, Sharepoint and Zendesk What We Offer Flexible working arrangements (remote) Opportunity to work in a high impact role at the intersection on AI, SaaS and Compliance / Regulatory intelligence Continuous learning and professional development How to Apply If you are excited about this opportunity and believe you have the skills and qualifications to excel as our Customer Success Manager, please submit your resume for our consideration. We appreciate all applications, but only selected candidates will be contacted for an interview. Thank you for considering joining the RegASK team. We look forward to reviewing your application!

content.title: Strategic Cloud Partner Manager | Remote | US at Grafana Labs
content.description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X. We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity Lead cloud partnership growth across AMER with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Work closely with the Head of the AMER Partner organization to align cloud initiatives with regional strategy. Build a scalable, repeatable cloud go-to-market motion across AMER in collaboration with CSP field teams, solution engineers, and SI partners. Drive joint business acceleration by deepening engagement with the region’s major cloud ecosystems. What You’ll Be Doing Developing and executing the AMER cloud partner strategy aligned to global cloud priorities. Building strong field relationships with AWS, GCP, and Azure to support co-selling, account alignment, and joint pursuit activity. Creating partner-sourced pipeline by educating cloud teams and activating CSP channels as a business-generation engine. Delivering enablement programs, workshops, and technical training for CSP sales and technical teams across APJ. Orchestrating joint go-to-market initiatives with cloud providers and SI partners, including events, campaigns, workshops, and customer-success projects. Managing operational elements of cloud partnerships such as Marketplace transactions, cloud credits, co-marketing funds, and program compliance. Integrating cloud-partnership activities with APJ sales, partner, marketing, and product teams. Tracking and reporting partner activity, co-sell pipeline, and performance metrics. Monitoring regional cloud-market trends to inform ongoing strategy. What Makes You a Great Fit 6–10+ years’ experience in AMER partner, alliances, or cloud sales roles within enterprise software, SaaS, or cloud technology companies. Hands-on experience running joint go-to-market and co-sell motions with AWS, GCP, or Azure. Proven ability to generate new opportunities through structured cloud-field engagement. Strong capability in delivering training and enablement across diverse AMER audiences. Excellent relationship-building skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders internally and externally. Confident managing pipeline, forecasting, and reporting. Comfortable working across distributed teams and multiple time zones. Bonus Points For Experience with cloud marketplaces, incentives, co-marketing funds, and programmatic partnership operations. Understanding of AMER SI, consulting, and cloud-native partner ecosystems. Background in high-growth SaaS or cloud-platform environments. Compensation & Rewards: In the United States, the OTE compensation range for this role is $258,000 - $280,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs’ success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow. Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings. #LI-Remote For information about how your personal data is used once you’ve applied to a job, check out our privacy policy.

content.title: Senior/Staff/Principal Technical Product Manager (U.S. Air Force) at Skylight
content.description: About Skylight Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services. We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world. If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists. The work we do matters. About the job At Skylight, product managers are responsible for strategy, planning, execution, stakeholder management, and team health. Product managers partner with researchers, designers, engineers, client stakeholders, and others to inform their product decisions. At a high level, it’s the product manager’s job to figure out what to build next and why. A technical product manager specializes in products with significant technical depth — platforms, APIs, data systems, or modernization efforts — where product decisions depend on fluency with the underlying architecture and engineering tradeoffs. Skylight has partnered with the U.S. Air Force across multiple legacy modernization efforts. The work spans modernization of legacy systems, new capability development in multi-vendor environments, iteration on established platforms, all inside an agile transformation and broader organizational change. You’ll own product direction for a legacy modernization effort where the architecture, integrations, and vendor landscape shape what’s possible. Expect to make the technical tradeoffs legible to stakeholders, pair closely with your government partners, and put AI-assisted ways of working to use across the team. What to know going in Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning the client’s domain and organization, and enabling your government partners. Access to users varies from team to team, so you’ll need to get creative about how you reach them. The client is early- to mid-transformation, so expect organizational and operational change along the way. This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit. What you’ll do Lead a cross-functional team of researchers, designers, engineers, and subject matter experts to build and ship high-impact products and services Translate needs from users and government partners into a product strategy, including vision, objectives, measures of success, product roadmap, and product backlog Manage the direction, scope, and priorities of the modernization effort, weighing architecture, integration, and migration tradeoffs alongside user needs Write user stories, prioritize stories, and build release plans Work in close partnership with government teams to transfer digital skills and product knowledge throughout the course of the project Creatively navigate bureaucratic challenges, paving the way for more intuitive processes in the future What we’re looking for Basic qualifications Understand lean product principles and how to apply them (e.g., minimum viable product) at various stages of the product life cycle in order to mitigate risk, validate assumptions, and amplify learning Can develop a product strategy that is informed by an understanding of the problem to be solved, prioritizes outcomes over feature sets, and establishes the direction of the product over time (e.g., product roadmap), including success criteria Ability to execute the product strategy by breaking down the product’s scope into usable chunks of value that can be realized sooner rather than later, creating and maintaining a prioritized backlog with validated user stories, and facilitating team ceremonies over the course of the product’s iterations Understand how to engage in the process of human-centered design in order to better inform product direction Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams Understand the merits of different software development methodologies (e.g., agile, lean) and how to put them into practice Enough technical fluency to weigh architecture and engineering tradeoffs with engineers and explain them to non-technical stakeholders Interest in mentoring, coaching, and pairing with government partners so they can carry the work forward Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values Nice-to-haves Military or government experience Experience leading legacy modernization efforts Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. Other requirements Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute. All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories. This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. You must be able to obtain and maintain a Common Access Card (CAC), which requires a favorable background check. You must complete a company background check successfully. Logistics Position type This is a full-time, exempt position. Location This is a fully remote position. Travel Expect occasional travel to Air Force bases across the U.S., quarterly at most. Expected start date November 2026 Care package Salary We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Product Manager at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows: Associate Product Manager: $90,000–$125,000 Product Manager I: $120,000–$140,000 Product Manager II: $135,000–$160,000 Senior Product Manager: $150,000–$185,000 Staff Product Manager: $170,000–$203,000 Principal Product Manager: $180,000–$230,000 Benefits Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways: Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance Short-term and long-term disability insurance Life and AD&D insurance Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options Business development / sales bonuses Referral bonuses Annual $2000 allowance for professional development Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more) Flexible, remote-friendly work environment An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good Interview tips Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview: Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works. Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them. Browse our case studies to learn more about our work. If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital. We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

content.title: Senior Business Strategist at Seer Interactive
content.description: Seer Interactive is a digital marketing consultancy that harnesses compassion, data, technology, and AI to make a mark on our communities, our coworkers, our clients, our industry, and our neighbors. We relentlessly pursue (and share) the truth, bringing together millions of data points from quantitative and qualitative sources, enhanced by responsible, human-centered AI. Our purpose is to unlock potential across these communities, envisioning a world where doing the right thing is intuitive and informed. At Seer, we see AI as a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and creativity. Regardless of your division or discipline, leveraging AI is a core part of how we deliver smarter, faster, and more strategic outcomes for our clients. Our AI Council drives company-wide integration by focusing on education, purposeful implementation, and continuous learning, ensuring that AI is embedded in how we think, operate, and grow. If you’re ready to uplift others, challenge your ego, commit to the truth, and be better than yesterday—keep reading. Seer is a remote-first agency and a Certified B-Corp, with team members across the country. If an office environment is more your style, this position can also sit in our HQ office in Philadelphia. We can only consider candidates based in the US who can work continental US-based hours. The Role: If the idea of dialing for dollars makes you want to close the tab, keep reading. This role isn’t that. You’re a digital marketing practitioner who has spent years building strategies, presenting to executives, and making the case for how channels work together to drive business outcomes. You’ve been selling your expertise all along but you just never called it sales. At Seer, you’ll take that instinct and apply it to one of the most intellectually honest growth practices in the industry: building (inbound) relationships with major brands, figuring out which ones we can actually help, and building the strategy to prove it. Role Highlights Lead Qualification & Consultative Discovery We have a pipeline of 600+ inbound leads annually, your job is to ask the right questions, get to the truth quickly, and be just as willing to disqualify a lead as you are to close it Run discovery calls with Fortune 500 marketing teams to understand their business challenges, channel mix, digital maturity, and what success actually looks like for them Strategy & Pitch Development Collaborate with divisional experts across SEO, Paid Media, Analytics, and Creative to build data-informed, channel-integrated growth strategies tailored to each prospect Lead pitch presentations and proposals for prospects up to the C-suite that show exactly how Seer can move the needle Negotiate and finalize contracts with legal guidance when deals are ready to close Pipeline & Client Handoff Manage the full process from first contact through client kick-off, ensuring every new partner is a strong values and capability fit before anything is signed Deliver a seamless handoff to account teams so every new client relationship starts on solid ground Thought Leadership & Community Contribute to the Seer blog, speak at industry events, and engage in professional communities to build Seer’s brand and surface new business conversations organically Essential Skills You have a depth of knowledge in digital marketing. You understand how SEO, paid media, analytics, and other channels interact to drive business outcomes, not just how one channel works in isolation You are a natural relationship builder who has spent your career earning trust with clients or stakeholders, not a stranger to a high-stakes conversation You have experience presenting strategy to senior decision-makers and can translate complexity into clarity for a VP or CMO audience You are comfortable operating autonomously with a high-volume workload and bring structure and discipline to your own pipeline You are data-driven, you use numbers to qualify, build your case, and sharpen your approach over time You feel energized by the consultative side of client work, you want to solve real problems, not pitch from a script You are comfortable with ambiguity and can make good decisions with incomplete information You have experience working with AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, or strategy development and you’re always looking for ways to work smarter Bonus! You have a background in Client Engagement, Account Management, or a client-facing strategy role and have been responsible for organic account growth You have experience in a digital agency environment where you’ve pitched or contributed to pitches for new clients You have familiarity with tools like Pipedrive, HubSpot, or LinkedIn Sales Navigator You have hands-on channel experience in more than one discipline (e.g., SEO + Paid, or Paid + Analytics) This might not be the right role for you if You thrive on cold outreach and commission-based incentives, this role is 90% inbound with a full salary and bonus, not a commission structure You specialize deeply in one digital marketing channel but haven’t had to make the case for how channels work together You prefer to stay in execution mode and aren’t energized by client-facing conversations or the business side of the work You need a highly defined playbook to follow: this role requires judgment, curiosity, and comfort with figuring things out in real time Saying “no” to a potential client feels like failure, here, disqualifying the wrong-fit lead is part of doing the job well 30/60/90 First 30 Days — Learn Immerse yourself in Seer’s pitch process, service offerings, and the types of leads we work best with Shadow discovery calls and strategy presentations to understand how the Business Strategy team qualifies and wins business Begin running your own discovery conversations with inbound leads under guidance 60 Days — Build Independently own the full discovery process on a set of inbound leads from first call through proposal Build your first pitch collaboratively with a divisional SME and present it to a real prospect Develop your working understanding of when to push forward and when a lead isn’t the right fit 90 Days — Lead Owning your pipeline end-to-end with a clear handle on close rate, average deal size, and time-to-close Contributing intelligence back to the team on patterns you’re seeing what kinds of leads convert, what objections come up, what the market is saying Tracking toward a $2M annual revenue target from inbound leads $120,000 - $150,000 a year OTE for this role is $120,000-150,000/year This OTE is base + bonus based on revenue attainment Your final offered compensation will be determined by your skills and experience Evaluation of comp at least once a year content.title: Staff/Principal Software Engineer, Consulting (U. S. Air Force) at Skylight
content.description: About Skylight Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services. We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world. If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists. The work we do matters. About the job At Skylight, software engineers design, implement, and maintain software systems to improve government services for users. This software is built to meet the needs of regular users of government services as well as Skylight’s partners in government. A consulting software engineer focuses on advisory engagements where the deliverable is guidance, assessment, or technical strategy rather than delivering code. Skylight has partnered with the U.S. Air Force across multiple legacy modernization efforts. The work spans modernization of legacy systems, new capability development in multi-vendor environments, iteration on established platforms, all inside an agile transformation and broader organizational change. You’ll assess legacy systems, shape the technical strategy for modernizing them, and pair directly with government engineers to raise the bar on how software gets built. Expect to spend your time in architecture reviews, working sessions with vendors and Air Force teams, and hands-on demonstrations of modern, AI-assisted engineering practices. What to know going in Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning the client’s domain and organization, and enabling your government partners. Access to users varies from team to team, so you’ll need to get creative about how you reach them. The client is early- to mid-transformation, so expect organizational and operational change along the way. This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit. What you’ll do Assess legacy applications and their technical environments to identify technical debt, instability, and other opportunities for improvement, then design, document, and communicate solutions Own the modernization strategy, technical direction, architectural decisions, and test strategy for the modernization, in collaboration with government engineers and partner vendors but accountable for the result Advocate for and model lean-agile engineering practices such as API-first design, simple design, continuous integration, version control, and automated testing Guide teams toward secure, compliant software that meets federal security standards and defends against common vulnerabilities Pair with and coach government engineers so modern practices, including AI-assisted development, stick after you’ve moved on Collaborate with product managers, researchers, and designers so technical recommendations serve user and mission needs What we’re looking for Basic qualifications Ability to write clean, working, and reusable code Understand the different pieces of software systems and how to fit them together, while keeping performance, reliability, and availability in mind Familiar with how to build secure, compliant software and defend against common vulnerabilities Experience evaluating existing systems and communicating technical findings and recommendations to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders Comfort holding architectural decision rights on a multi-vendor engagement, and making the tradeoffs legible to non-technical stakeholders Experience working in agile software development Interest in mentoring, coaching, and pairing with government partners so they can carry the work forward Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values Nice-to-haves Military or government experience Experience leading legacy modernization efforts or reverse-engineering legacy applications where the code, the documentation, and stakeholder knowledge don’t agree Experience with web-based tech stacks (e.g., Java/React) and cloud infrastructure Experience coaching other engineers on the failure modes of AI-assisted development Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. Other requirements Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute. All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories. This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. You must be able to obtain and maintain a Common Access Card (CAC), which requires a favorable background check. You must complete a company background check successfully. Logistics Position type This is a full-time, exempt position. Location This is a fully remote position. Travel Expect occasional travel to Air Force bases across the U.S., quarterly at most. Expected start date November 2026 Care package Salary We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Software Engineer at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows: Associate Software Engineer: $90,000–$125,000 Software Engineer I: $120,000–$140,000 Software Engineer II: $135,000–$160,000 Senior Software Engineer: $150,000–$185,000 Staff Software Engineer: $170,000–$203,000 Principal Software Engineer: $180,000–$230,000 Benefits Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways: Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance Short-term and long-term disability insurance Life and AD&D insurance Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options Business development / sales bonuses Referral bonuses Annual $2000 allowance for professional development Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more) Flexible, remote-friendly work environment An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good Interview tips Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview: Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works. Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them. Browse our case studies to learn more about our work. If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital. We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

content.title: Sales Development Representative, Group Sales at CSC Generation
content.description: Adventure is our Culture. Join a team that celebrates a lifestyle as bold as the terrain we love. At Backcountry, we are rooted in adventure, recognition, and wellbeing on and off the mountain. We spotlight employee stories, celebrate milestones, and offer exclusive outdoor perks. Whether you are at HQ, in a retail store, or remote, you will be part of a team that thrives on energy, exploration, and connection. This B2B program is growing and needs a driven, outbound-focused rep to build pipeline and fuel that growth. As Sales Development Representative, Group Sales , you will own the top of the funnel — prospecting, outreach, and qualification — running outbound campaigns across email, phone, and LinkedIn to identify and engage prospective group accounts. This role is a proven path into Account Management: reps who master outbound prospecting and consistently deliver qualified pipeline are the first considered as Account Manager openings come up. They take ownership, move fast, and want to see the direct impact of their work. Clear Growth Path: This role is the on-ramp to Account Management — your outbound results are your promotion case. Training and Development: Structured sales training and hands-on coaching from your manager accelerate your outbound craft. content.title: Senior Software Engineer, ASW Launch Ops at Zipline
content.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You and The Role Joining Zipline as a Senior Software Engineer on the ASW Launch Ops team , you will be part of the Application Software organization. You will build the operational platform that turns a new market from an idea into a live, revenue-generating network—covering site acquisition, infrastructure design, permitting, construction execution, deployment tracking, and launch readiness. This is a greenfield, high-ownership individual contributor role. You will help establish the technical foundations for a platform intended to scale Zipline from tens of sites to hundreds or thousands. Working directly with Real Estate, Launch Operations, Construction, Hardware, Flight Operations, Commercial, and Manufacturing, you will replace fragmented manual workflows with a unified, auditable, and automated operational system. Your work will directly affect Zipline’s ability to expand into new countries and reliably deliver time-critical supplies at scale. What You’ll Do Drive core product domains. Serve as a technical owner for critical capabilities across site acquisition, permitting, infrastructure design, construction execution, deployment tracking, and launch readiness—ensuring their long-term technical health and strategic direction. Deliver measurable impact. Reduce manual coordination, shorten site-launch timelines, improve launch-date predictability, and give cross-functional leaders clear visibility into execution, dependencies, and risk. Lead technical design. Define the APIs, data models, service boundaries, and architectural patterns that power the platform, with a focus on maintainability, auditability, observability, and pragmatic evolution. Build durable operational workflows. Translate complex real-world processes into software that supports long-running workflows, government and vendor interactions, physical assets, documents and permits, approvals, dependencies, state transitions, and exception handling. Create a unified operational source of truth. Build resilient integrations across ERP, GIS, document management, permitting, construction and project management, asset management, and internal operational systems. Design for the people doing the work. Partner directly with users to turn fragmented processes and data into intuitive tools for planning and execution. Prototype workflows, validate them in real operating environments, and drive adoption. Own production excellence. Build and operate business-critical services with meaningful health metrics, SLOs, observability, runbooks, and recovery mechanisms. Participate in on-call, lead incident response when needed, and improve systems through thoughtful postmortems. Remain deeply hands-on. Ship production code, review critical changes, troubleshoot complex system behavior, and follow major capabilities from discovery through deployment and operation. Lead through influence. Create clarity in ambiguous problem spaces, identify systemic risks and cross-team dependencies, and drive alignment across technical and operational stakeholders. Elevate the team. Mentor peers, raise engineering standards, and strengthen practices in system design, automated testing, CI/CD, operational reliability, and pragmatic delivery. What You’ll Bring Senior individual contribution. At least 5 years of professional experience developing and maintaining full-stack production systems at scale, or demonstrated equivalent technical mastery. Product-minded engineering. You understand user needs, identify root causes, and design pragmatic solutions that balance business value, usability, technical simplicity, and long-term maintainability. Systems perspective. You can break down ambiguous operational problems, collaborate with stakeholders to define the right solution, and deliver software that improves real-world processes. Strong technical fundamentals. You design maintainable systems, model data thoughtfully, create robust APIs, and make sound tradeoffs across frontend applications, backend services, distributed systems, and infrastructure. Complex workflow experience. You have modeled long-running workflows, external dependencies, physical assets, and complex state transitions with strong auditability, observability, and failure recovery. Integration experience. You have built reliable integrations between internal services and external or enterprise systems. Experience with ERP, GIS, document management, construction, permitting, or asset management systems is valuable but not required. Modern technology mindset. You are comfortable learning and working across technologies such as Python, Go, PostgreSQL, React, Kafka, gRPC, AWS, Grafana, and Honeycomb. We value engineers who learn new tools quickly over experience with every specific technology. Effective use of AI. You use AI thoughtfully throughout the development lifecycle—including design, implementation, testing, debugging, and code review—while maintaining strong engineering judgment and quality. Operational excellence. You define meaningful service-health metrics and reliability goals, create actionable runbooks, participate in on-call rotations, and drive improvements through incident reviews. Quantifiable results. You have shipped high-impact capabilities that reduce manual intervention, shorten cycle times, increase predictability, improve throughput, or strengthen reliability—and can demonstrate the results with concrete metrics. Cross-functional leadership. You communicate clearly under ambiguity, prioritize decisively, and influence stakeholders across engineering and operational organizations without relying on formal authority. Owner’s mindset. You balance speed with correctness and understand the real operational consequences of software used to deploy physical infrastructure and support safety-critical operations. Assuming this position, you will take meaningful ownership of a business-critical operational platform from day one. Your mandate is to deliver quantifiable improvements in launch velocity, predictability, execution visibility, and system reliability while building foundations capable of supporting Zipline’s continued global expansion. What Else You Need To Know This role can be based in South San Francisco or remotely within the United States. Regular travel is expected so that you can work closely with stakeholders, understand operational challenges firsthand, and build software grounded in real-world workflows. Travel may include visits to Zipline headquarters, operating sites, and new-market launches. Remote team members should expect more frequent travel—typically a few days at a time, potentially once per month. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

content.title: Account Executive - Fully Remote at Sowelo Consulting sp. z o.o.
content.description: Do you have a proven track record of consistently exceeding ARR quotas within the SaaS, supply chain, logistics, or EDI sectors? Ready to join a global leader transforming the retail supply chain while enjoying the flexibility of a fully remote UK role? Great, please read on as we have a role for you! You could join the world’s leading retail network, connecting trading partners around the globe to optimize supply chain operations for all retail partners. They support data-driven partnerships with innovative cloud technology, customer-obsessed service and accessible experts so their customers can focus on what they do best. To date, more than 120,000 companies in retail, grocery, distribution, supply, and logistics have chosen Our Client as their retail network. You will join our clients Sales team where you are responsible for strategically driving new revenue by systematically prospecting, developing, and closing opportunities across the assigned territory.You will be partnering with the Sales Engineering team during the pre-sales process and ensuring a smooth transition of new customers to the Implementation team. Post-onboarding you will retain the customer accounts to actively identify and execute upsell and cross-sell opportunities, ultimately aiming to both acquire new enterprise customers and expand business with the existing client base. Your tasks will include: Own the full sales cycle within a defined territory, driving a prescriptive sales process to identify, prospect, develop, and close new business opportunities and achieve Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) targets. Proactively prospect for new clients and nurture qualified leads generated by marketing and other teams. Maximize revenue from the existing customer base through strategic cross-selling and upselling initiatives. Accurately manage a rolling 90-day sales pipeline in Salesforce, documenting all key activities and insights to ensure quota attainment. Collaborate closely with the broader account team and Customer Success to leverage relationships, ensure high customer satisfaction, and drive seamless post-sale alignment. To be a good fit for the Account Executive Role, you will have: Minimum of 2 years of relevant IT sales, preferably in a B2B environment, ideally within the supply chain, EDI, logistics, ERP companies, with experience in commission-based sales roles. Proven ability to deliver compelling and persuasive sales presentations that clearly articulate the value proposition of complex products/solutions to diverse business stakeholders. Exceptional communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written), with the ability to effectively translate complex business issues and technical details for audiences with varying levels of expertise. Demonstrated capacity to take full ownership of the sales cycle from initial lead to deal closure, requiring minimal supervision. content.title: Senior Technical Program Manager - Credit & Lending at Mercury
content.description: Mercury is building Mercury Bank, N.A., a proposed nationally chartered bank focused on serving ambitious businesses. Credit and lending are central to that mission, and as we migrate our charge card and term loan products to the Bank’s own balance sheet and build the next generation of lending infrastructure, we need someone who can hold the full program together. The Senior Technical Program Manager for Credit and Lending will own end-to-end delivery of the technology programs that power Mercury’s charge card, term loan, and adjacent credit products. You will be the connective tissue between Engineering, Product, Risk, Compliance, Treasury, and Operations: setting strategy for how these programs run, surfacing tradeoffs that unblock leaders, sequencing the critical path, and ensuring that what ships is audit-ready from day one. We are looking for someone who has operated at this level before, in a regulated environment, at scale, with real accountability for outcomes. *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC. What you’ll do: Program ownership Own the integrated program plan across all active credit and lending workstreams, covering milestones, dependencies, and critical paths across Engineering, Product, Risk, Compliance, Treasury, and Operations. Proactively manage sequencing, resourcing tradeoffs, and escalations. When initiatives are off-track, you identify it first and bring a recommended path forward. Ensure Compliance, Treasury, and Operations readiness lands alongside product and regulatory milestones Drive incident learnings back into design, test coverage, and runbooks so each issue improves the underlying system, not just fixes the symptom. Contribute to the overall (proposed) Mercury Bank, NA technical program, collaborating with other TPMs to build a holistic view of progress and risks Governance and decision-making Keep a single source of truth for status, decisions, risks, and owners. Maintain a living RAID log with clear owners and impact assessments. Facilitate structured decision-making by surfacing options and tradeoffs to leaders before problems escalate. Build and improve the operating systems that drive credit and lending product decisions: planning cycles, reviews, decision frameworks, launch readiness. Communication and influence Produce concise, predictable updates calibrated to the audience. Synthesize complex cross-functional information into recommendations that help executives decide and move. Produce documentation of program objectives, architecture decisions, and operational impacts that onboards new team members without requiring a meeting to explain it. Function as a trusted thought partner to engineering leads, product managers, and senior leadership. Execution and improvement Identify inefficiencies and eliminate them through automation, AI tooling, or process redesign. Lead technical retrospectives and post-mortems, ensuring learnings are systematized rather than forgotten. What we’re looking for: Experience 10+ years of program management or technical program management in a high-growth or regulated environment. Direct experience in financial services, fintech, or credit infrastructure. Compliance, audit, reporting and risk management obligations are familiar territory. Track record of operating at the department or business level, owning programs with multiple concurrent workstreams and cross-functional accountability. Proven ability to communicate with and influence executive stakeholders, in writing and in high-stakes meetings, without a senior manager to translate. Bonus: Familiarity with the lending tooling ecosystem such as loan origination, credit risk management and lending management systems. How you work Product-first. You evaluate everything through: what is the user problem, what is the fastest path to learning, what actually moves the needle. AI-native. You use AI tools to do your actual work. You have built workflows or tooling that changed how your team operates. When you see a repetitive process, you automate it. Comfortable in ambiguity. You build structure where there is none. Systems thinker. You see dependencies, second-order effects, and points of failure before they surface, and you build programs that account for them. Energized by building and operating. You do your best work designing the system and running it well once it is built. What you bring: Technical fluency. You can understand and challenge engineering decisions, identify technical risks early, and translate complexity for non-technical stakeholders. Exceptional written and verbal communication. You write documentation that clarifies hard decisions and build frameworks teams actually adopt. Commercial instincts. You understand the financial dynamics of a lending business well enough to evaluate tradeoffs with authority. High emotional intelligence. You build trust quickly across engineering, product, risk, and executive stakeholders. You navigate complex interpersonal situations without losing credibility or momentum. content.title: People AI & Automation Engineer at Deepgram
content.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. About the Role We are building the next generation of People Operations at Deepgram. We’re looking for an early-career engineer to partner directly with our Head of People to identify, design, and build AI-powered workflows that fundamentally change how People Ops operates. You will not be maintaining an HRIS or administering traditional People systems. You will build the systems that sit on top of them. You’ll take manual, repetitive, high-friction People processes and turn them into intelligent workflows using AI, automation, APIs, internal tools, and agents. You’ll work across People, Engineering, IT, and other functions to build secure, scalable solutions that allow employees and managers to get answers and complete workflows without requiring a People team member for every interaction. This is a highly hands-on role for someone who loves building, experimenting, and finding ways to make work dramatically more efficient. What You’ll Do Partner directly with the People & Talent Team to identify high-impact opportunities to apply AI and automation across People Operations. Build an AI-first onboarding experience that is scalable, up to date, and provides an exceptional experience. Turn manual People workflows into automated, AI-powered systems. Build AI agents and workflows that can answer questions, gather information, initiate processes, and complete defined actions. Integrate AI systems with existing tools, including HRIS, Slack, recruiting, performance, compensation, and other internal systems. Build internal tools and interfaces that make People processes dramatically easier for employees, managers, and the People team. Prototype quickly, test with real users, learn from what works, and iterate. Establish appropriate human-in-the-loop controls, escalation paths, permissions, and safeguards for sensitive People workflows. Partner with Engineering and IT on architecture, security, access controls, and productionizing successful prototypes. Measure whether what you build actually saves time, improves the employee experience, or increases the quality and consistency of People Operations. Notice : We’re aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @ deepgram.com email address. If you’ve received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

content.title: Toptal : Professional Photoshop Artists
content.description: Headquarters: Remote URL: https://www.toptal.com/ About the Role Our client is building an open dataset of real, professional Photoshop work, published on HuggingFace under CC-BY-4.0, to evaluate how well AI systems understand creative editing. Not synthetic tasks. Not staged demos. Actual production work, done the way you already do it. We're looking for working Photoshop artists across six disciplines to complete client-style briefs while a screen recorder captures the session. You work from a brief, you open Photoshop, you do the job. Each task runs roughly 1–3 hours. Your process is the product here. The layer decisions, the masking approach, the moment you undo three steps and take a different route - that's exactly the signal this dataset is built to capture. If you've ever thought AI evaluation of creative work is shallow because the people building it have never actually retouched a beauty shot or built a matte painting, this is your chance to fix that. Rate: $25/hr USD Timeline: This is an extremely urgent role with work starting immediately. If you are interested and apply, please expect to be contacted and requested to complete your account setup on September 9th (Friday), 10th (Saturday), or the 11th (Sunday) to be considered for this role. What You'll Do Complete Photoshop tasks from a client-provided creative brief, working at your normal professional standard Run a client-provided session recorder for the full duration of each task Deliver layered, production-quality PSDs along with final output Work independently, at your own pace, within the scope of each brief Contribute work that will be published openly for research use What You Bring We're recruiting across six specializations and aiming for balanced coverage. Tell us which one is your home turf: Matte painting / digital environments Key visual / campaign compositing Game & UI assets Print & packaging pre-press Portrait / beauty retouching E-commerce / product retouching Hard requirements - please read carefully: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) with your own licensed copy of Photoshop. Intel Macs and Windows machines cannot be used for this engagement. Photoshop only. No Illustrator, Nuke, Blender, Procreate, or iPad workflows in the captured session. No generative AI of any kind - no Generative Fill, no Firefly, no third-party generative plugins. All work must be manually executed. Individual contributor. No teams, studios, or subcontracted work. Comfortable publishing openly under CC-BY-4.0, meaning the resulting work and session data will be freely available for anyone to use with attribution. Demonstrable professional portfolio in at least one of the six categories above. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toptal-professional-photoshop-artists

content.title: GeoPro Labs Inc: Head of Operations - Shopify App Portfolio
content.description: Headquarters: Victoria, British Columbia, Canada URL: https://geoproapp.com The opportunity I'm looking for an experienced operator to take ownership of a portfolio of three established Shopify apps with a combined ARR of approximately $1.87M. The portfolio includes: Geo:Pro: Geolocation-based storefront personalization TrackiPal: PayPal tracking automation for Shopify merchants Easy Lockdown: Content and storefront access control Together, these are profitable, well-established products with engaged customer bases. They're not hypergrowth startups, but well-run businesses with clear opportunities to improve the product experience, strengthen operations and continue growing over time. As the portfolio has grown, it's reached the point where I need an experienced operator to lead the day-to-day, keep the business running smoothly and turn strategy into execution. The role is fully remote, async-friendly and suited to someone who enjoys ownership, autonomy and building well-run businesses. What you'd own Team coordination and delivery: Run the day-to-day by coordinating the developer and tester through the full delivery cycle - from spec → build → ship → measure - keeping everyone aligned across time zones and hiring additional contractors as needed. Roadmap and prioritization: We'll set the roadmap together. I'll be closely involved at first, and over time this becomes increasingly your call. Turn Amplitude data, review themes and support signals into a prioritized backlog in Linear, and write clear tickets for the developer. Metrics and experimentation: Own the analytics story. Understand what moved, what didn't and what to try next. Design experiments and report on impact. Quality and documentation: Continually raise the bar on user experience through better documentation, smoother onboarding, fewer rough edges. Platform stewardship: Stay ahead of Shopify API changes, manage App Store compliance reviews and lead our annual Built for Shopify review to retain BFS status. Support oversight and escalations: Our support agency handles tier-1 tickets. You're the escalation point for product and engineering issues and own the agency relationship, ensuring response times, ticket quality and the merchant experience meet the bar. Shopify App Store Paid Ads: Oversee existing paid advertising campaigns, working with our marketing contractor to ensure everything runs smoothly. We'll set the marketing budget together each quarter, and you'll manage it. Shopify App Store rankings: Monitor Shopify App Store rankings across the portfolio, identify opportunities to improve rankings and respond quickly when rankings decline. What you don't have to do Write code (there's a developer for that) Do QA (there's a tester for that) Handle routine support tickets (an agency handles that) Respond to reviews (a contractor handles that) Fundraise, hire executives, sit in stakeholder meetings or manage political overhead - none of that exists here Growth areas we've already identified Easy Lockdown: Shift to usage-based pricing Geo:Pro + Easy Lockdown: Onboarding and activation optimization Geo:Pro + Easy Lockdown: Feature gaps that address missing customer use cases All three apps: Lift review ratings to improve organic App Store rankings You're not walking into a blank page - there's already a clear direction, but plenty of room to test your own ideas. What you'll be walking into Small, remote team: You'll be coordinating a small team of contractors working across different time zones, so communication and keeping work moving are a big part of the role. Established products: The apps are profitable and well established, but some of the codebases are older and occasionally require pragmatic workarounds rather than perfect solutions. Data-driven decisions: Our analytics stack is solid (Amplitude, BigQuery, Shopify Partners) - SQL fluency, or comfort writing it with AI help, is required. How we'll work together Founder involvement: I've run these apps alongside another business and know them inside out. I'll stay focused on product direction, strategy, quarterly planning and major decisions while you run the day-to-day. Working rhythm: We'll meet weekly at first while we build context and alignment, then move to monthly strategy check-ins and quarterly planning sessions. Beyond that, you'll have the autonomy to run with it. Who you are Strong operator: You've successfully run product or delivery for a small SaaS team. Background isn't important - results are. Technically fluent: You can write clear product specs, understand trade-offs and weigh development estimates without needing to review code. Organized and proactive: You enjoy coordinating people, removing blockers and making sure nothing falls through the cracks. Data-driven: You use Amplitude, SQL and customer feedback to inform decisions. Self-directed: You're comfortable working asynchronously, managing your own priorities and taking ownership without constant direction. Bonus: Experience in the Shopify ecosystem, App Store Optimization (ASO), paid acquisition or SaaS growth. Where this could go This isn't a role with a fixed ceiling. As you build context, take on more responsibility and the portfolio grows, there's scope for the role to grow too. Exactly what that looks like will depend on the business and the impact you have, but the door is genuinely open. Role details Time: Part-time, approximately 15-25 hours per week Compensation: US$65-$85/hour, depending on experience Employment: Contractor or employee - whichever works best for you Location: Fully remote, async-friendly, any timezone Start: As soon as you're available How to apply If this sounds like a role you'd enjoy, send me a 3-5 minute Loom walking me through how you'd approach your first 90 days. Assume you've had one week to get oriented - what would you focus on first, what would you want to understand, and how would you decide what to work on? Email your Loom to: apply@geoproapp.com I'll personally review every application. If your Loom is a strong fit, I'll invite you to a short introductory interview. If that goes well, we'll schedule a final, more in-depth interview before making an offer. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/geopro-labs-inc-head-of-operations-shopify-app-portfolio
